svg.title: Where the money goes
svg.text: Billed after the procedure, for example $100
The anaesthetist submits the List and the office
authorises it: only then does billing start.
A receivable from the billable party, linked to a
payable to the anaesthetist who did the List.
The billable party pays $100 into AA's trust bank
account, and the receivable is cleared.
AA owes the anaesthetist only what has been paid:
the payable waits for the money to come in.
The payable is authorised for what was received,
so it joins the next payables run.
The payables run pays Dr Nick out of the trust
account. Everything nets back to zero.
When the payables run happens (OQ-47) and when
the buyer-created tax invoice is raised (OQ-29).
Invoiced before the procedure, for example $200
The Booking is on a prepaid Contract. An admin
approves the invoice (a step AA can switch off).
Pair to the AA Holding account
A receivable from the payer, linked to a payable
to the AA Holding account, not the anaesthetist.
The payer pays $200 into the same trust bank
account. It waits there: no anaesthetist is paid.
The procedure is done. Which event releases the
money, the List authorised or the procedure
Transfer to whoever did the List
A journal transfer, not a payment: no money moves
in the bank. The debt moves to the anaesthetist.
The payables run pays Dr Ben out of the trust
account, the same as any other payable.
Unpaid: the invoice is credited. Paid: refunded
in full from the AA Holding account. Both happen
automatically as part of the cancellation.
One trust bank account holds all of it. Control accounts hold
totals; their sub-ledgers hold the detail, and each sub-ledger
must add up to its control account.
Every payment in and every payment out, prepaid or not.
Analysed out into who is due to be paid.
A creditor beside the anaesthetists, a "fake anaesthetist": not a
bank account and not a Xero ledger account. Its balance is every
prepayment received for a procedure not yet done. It is never paid
itself, and only the system moves money out of it: a transfer to
whoever did the List, or a refund.
+ adds to what is held or owed, − takes it away.
Same trust account, same pairs: a prepayment's payable waits with the AA Holding account until the procedure is done, then moves by transfer
